name: Semaglutide
summary: A GLP-1 receptor agonist that improves glycemic control and drives weight loss largely through appetite and gastric-emptying effects.
good: Patients where weight loss plus glycemic improvement are both important.
bad: Significant GI intolerance or suspected gastric-emptying problems.
clinicalPearls: Dose escalation is part of tolerability engineering, not just a formality.
mechanism: Enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, and reduces appetite.
indications: Type 2 diabetes and obesity management in appropriately selected patients.
interactionNotes: GI slowing can alter timing of other oral drugs; hydration and titration strategy matter.

warnings: Nausea, vomiting, constipation, and gastroparesis-like symptoms are common limiting issues.
